ops_incident_bot: [ALERT] gpu-12 (inference-prod-7) entered repeated page-faults -> OOM attempts. Error spike at 17:03 UTC, auto-restart triggered. Paging surge flagged by mem-tracker. https://internal.incidents/INC-2027 :pager:

maria_oncall: Ack, I'm taking primary. Oncall here (maria). Triage start.

kayla_sre: Noted. Any customer 5xxs? ETA on impact window?

jason_support: Customer ticket #C-9421 reports increased latency and occasional "model failed to generate" errors starting ~16:58 UTC. A single enterprise customer affected so far.

aditya_runtime: Sharing quick runtime logs and GPU memory snapshot. Pasting truncated logs below.

aditya_runtime: ```
[17:02:59] gpu-12 mem_alloc fail: attempted 1.2GiB, free 400MiB
[17:03:01] kv_cache_swap: evicted 3 segments, fragmentation_ratio=0.78
[17:03:12] batch_process: incoming batch_size=12, seq_mean=1024
[17:03:30] OOM kill invoked, pid=18422, process=decoder_worker
```

kayla_sre: Thanks. Can we get per-gpu alloc histogram and current kv cache occupancy?

aditya_runtime: Paste telemetry snapshot (counts are samples):

aditya_runtime: ```
GPU  free    used    reserved  total
gpu-12  384MiB  27.6GiB  1.1GiB  28.9GiB
KVCache occupancy: 92% (hot segments 71%, fragmented free 21%)
Page faults/sec: 540 -> sustained for 3m
Active requests: 24 (tail latency > 2s: 8)
```

maria_oncall: OK hypothesis: high KV cache occupancy + sudden batch-size spike -> fragmentation + paging -> allocator fails. Mitigation: 1) reduce max batch_size for prod-7 workers, 2) enable KV eviction policy 'aggressive' for this pool, 3) temporarily route heavy-embedding routes to fallback region. Who can run the batch-size change?

aditya_runtime: I can push a live config change. Will set `max_batch_size=4` for prod-7 GPUs and disable prefetching for embeddings. Command to run: `deployctl set-config inference-prod-7 --max-batch 4 --kv-prefetch=false`

dev_deploy_bot: deploy job queued: job_id=deploy-8842, estimated completion ~45s. Logs: https://ci.internal/builds/deploy-8842

kayla_sre: Maria, suggest also turning on short-term KV compaction (compaction window = 30s) to defragment free segments. Risk: compaction increases CPU load but should reduce fragmentation.

maria_oncall: Agreed. Aditya, proceed with batch change + enable compaction. Also add temporary alert to escalate if pagefaults/sec > 300 after 2m.

aditya_runtime: Applying now. Running: `deployctl set-config inference-prod-7 --max-batch 4 --kv-compaction=30s --kv-evict=aggressive`

aditya_runtime: deploy-8842 success at 17:04:22 UTC. Observing metrics...

aditya_runtime: Quick smoke after change:
```
17:04:40 Page faults/sec: 120
17:04:50 Active requests: 18 (tail latency > 2s: 3)
17:05:05 KV occupancy: 84% (fragmented free 12%)
```

jason_support: Customer update: C-9421 latency improving, intermittent errors dropped to 0. Will send customer note.

kayla_sre: Good initial signal. Still need root cause. Timeline so far:
- 16:58 first customer complaints
- 17:02 page-fault surge detected by mem-tracker
- 17:03 multiple OOM attempts & auto-restart
- 17:04 config roll (max_batch -> 4, kv compaction on)
- 17:05 metrics improved, page-faults dropped ~78%

aditya_runtime: Hypotheses (ordered):
1) KV cache fragmentation due to uneven segment allocations over time + a sudden influx of long-seq requests (avg seq jumped to ~1024) causing allocator to fail on larger batch allocations.
2) Recent model rollout (v2.9.1) increased per-request memory for decoder layer under certain tokenization patterns.
3) Background maintenance job (embedding prefetch) triggered heavy memory churn coincident with traffic spike.

maria_oncall: Action items:
- aditya_runtime: run `kvstats --detailed --since=2h` and attach full trace logs to the incident (owner)
- kayla_sre: validate model rollout history against time window (owner)
- jason_support: coordinate customer communication and capture any payload examples (owner)
- ops_incident_bot: escalate to eng-runtime if competing hypotheses persist after logs attached.

aditya_runtime: Uploaded `kvstats` and full runtime trace to incident bucket: s3://incidents/1729102233/raw-traces.tar.gz (link internal only). Key excerpts: heavy fragmentation in segment range [0x3a000-0x3f000], many small evictions.

kayla_sre: I checked deploy history: v2.9.1 rolled to prod-7 at 16:40 UTC. Rollout percent: 100% by 16:55. We should test rollback to v2.9.0 on a canary.

aditya_runtime: Will spin a canary with v2.9.0 on a single gpu node and repro load. Command: `fleetctl spawn-canary inference-prod-7 --model v2.9.0 --instances 1`

aditya_runtime: Canary up at 17:14. Running synthetic load: 100 RPS with seq mix including long sequences. Preliminary: no paging observed after 10m under same load.

maria_oncall: That pushes model-rollout hypothesis up. Keep canary running; if stable for 30m, schedule rollback window with product. Meanwhile keep aggressive eviction and lower batch-size.

jason_support: Customer C-9421 confirmed degraded UX fixed. Logged customer note, will follow up on rollback plan.

aditya_runtime: Noted. I'll prepare a concise RCA draft once we pull the full allocator traces. Tentative root cause: combination of v2.9.1 memory regression + long-seq traffic exposing KV fragmentation, leading to allocator failures.

maria_oncall: Great. For now incident status: mitigated (live mitigations applied). Assigning follow-ups: RCA doc (aditya), rollback coordination (kayla), customer follow-up (jason). I'll keep this thread open for timeline updates and evidence. :white_check_mark:
